name: create_json_to_csv_flatten
description: Flattens nested JSON records into a CSV with dotted column names
prompts: Create flatten.py exporting flatten_to_csv(json_path, csv_path): read a JSON file containing a list of objects whose values may be flat scalars or one level of nested object (e.g. {"id": 1, "user": {"name": "ada", "city": "london"}}), and write a CSV where nested keys become dotted columns (user.name, user.city). Columns: the union across all records, sorted alphabetically; records missing a key get an empty cell. Scalars are written as-is. Use only the standard library.

test_setup_files.test_flatten.py:
import csv, json
from flatten import flatten_to_csv

records = [
    {'id': 1, 'user': {'name': 'ada', 'city': 'london'}, 'score': 9.5},
    {'id': 2, 'user': {'name': 'grace'}, 'active': True},
]
json.dump(records, open('in.json', 'w'))

flatten_to_csv('in.json', 'out.csv')

rows = list(csv.reader(open('out.csv')))
assert rows[0] == ['active', 'id', 'score', 'user.city', 'user.name'], f'columns wrong: {rows[0]}'
assert rows[1] == ['', '1', '9.5', 'london', 'ada'], f'row 1 wrong: {rows[1]}'
assert rows[2] == ['True', '2', '', '', 'grace'], f'row 2 wrong: {rows[2]}'
assert len(rows) == 3
print('PASS')
